name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_KINGDOM_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q01 - Basic principles of plant kingdom classification systems

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: In Whittaker's Five Kingdom system, cyanobacteria are placed in Kingdom Monera.

Statement II: Linnaeus gave an artificial system of classification based mainly on vegetative characters or androecium structure.

Statement III: George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker gave a natural classification system for flowering plants.

Statement IV: Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, and largely aquatic organisms.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Statement
Whittaker placed prokaryotic organisms including cyanobacteria in Kingdom Monera, excluding them from Kingdom Plantae.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Linnaeus introduced an artificial system that utilized gross superficial vegetative morphology and the structure of the androecium.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Bentham and Hooker developed a natural classification system for flowering plants taking into account internal ultrastructure, anatomy, embryology, and phytochemistry.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement and Synthesis
Algae are autotrophic, simple, thalloid organisms possessing photosynthetic pigments that flourish primarily in aquatic habitats.

Final Answer:
All four statements are correct: cyanobacteria belong to Kingdom Monera, Linnaeus gave an artificial system, Bentham and Hooker gave a natural system, and algae are simple autotrophic thalloid organisms.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I and Statement IV only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_KINGDOM_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q02 - Economic importance and major classes of algae

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: At least a half of the total carbon dioxide fixation on Earth is carried out by algae through photosynthesis.

Statement II: Agar obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria is used to grow microbes and in preparations of ice-creams and jellies.

Statement III: Algin is a commercial hydrocolloid harvested exclusively from red algae.

Statement IV: The algae are divided into three main classes: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, and Rhodophyceae.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Statement
Photosynthetic algae perform at least fifty percent of the total carbon dioxide fixation on Earth, contributing substantially to global primary productivity.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Agar is a phycocolloid extracted from the red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria, widely employed in culture media and food preparation.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Algin is produced by brown algae (Phaeophyceae), whereas carrageen is produced by red algae (Rhodophyceae); claiming algin comes from red algae is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement and Synthesis
Algae are taxonomically divided into Chlorophyceae (green algae), Phaeophyceae (brown algae), and Rhodophyceae (red algae).

Final Answer:
The first, second, and fourth statements are correct, while the third statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_KINGDOM_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q03 - Morphological and cytological features of Chlorophyceae

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: Green algae are usually grass green due to the dominance of pigments chlorophyll a and b.

Statement II: Pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts contain protein besides starch.

Statement III: The cell wall of Chlorophyceae consists of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.

Statement IV: Asexual zoospores in green algae bear 2 unequal flagella attached laterally to the cell body.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Statement
Chlorophyceae members exhibit a vivid grass-green colour because their chloroplasts are rich in chlorophyll a and b.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Pyrenoids are discrete intra-chloroplastic bodies storing starch surrounding a central proteinaceous core.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Statement
The cellulosic wall of green algae has a two-layered organization: an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement and Synthesis
Zoospores of green algae possess 2 to 8 equal flagella inserted apically, whereas two unequal lateral flagella are diagnostic of brown algae.

Final Answer:
The first, second, and third statements are correct, while the fourth statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_KINGDOM_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q04 - Comparative biochemistry of brown and red algae

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: Brown algae possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids, and the xanthophyll pigment fucoxanthin.

Statement II: In Phaeophyceae, reserve food is stored as complex carbohydrates in the form of laminarin or mannitol.

Statement III: Red algae store food as floridean starch, which is structurally very similar to amylopectin and glycogen.

Statement IV: Red algae reproduce asexually by flagellated motile zoospores with apical flagella.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Statement
Phaeophyceae contain chlorophyll a and c along with fucoxanthin, which gives them their characteristic olive green to brown shades.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Photosynthetic reserves in brown algae are stored as complex carbohydrates, notably laminarin and mannitol.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Rhodophyceae store carbohydrates as floridean starch, an alpha-glucan showing close structural homology to amylopectin and glycogen.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement and Synthesis
Red algae lack flagella and motile stages entirely throughout their life cycle; their asexual spores and gametes are non-motile.

Final Answer:
The first, second, and third statements are correct, while the fourth statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_KINGDOM_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q05 - Life cycle stages and ecology of bryophytes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: Bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because they require water for sexual reproduction.

Statement II: The predominant phase of the bryophyte life cycle is the independent haploid gametophyte.

Statement III: The sporophyte in bryophytes is free-living and completely independent of the gametophyte.

Statement IV: Mosses form dense mats on the soil that reduce the impact of falling rain and prevent soil erosion.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Statement
Bryophytes live in soil but depend on an external film of water for flagellated antherozoids to swim to the archegonium.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Statement
The dominant, persistent, photosynthetic plant body in bryophytes is the haploid gametophytic generation.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Statement
The bryophyte sporophyte is physically attached to and derives organic nourishment from the photosynthetic gametophyte, lacking an independent existence.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement and Synthesis
Carpet-like moss mats cushion raindrops, protect soil structure, and play a major ecological role in reducing soil erosion.

Final Answer:
The first, second, and fourth statements are correct, while the third statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_KINGDOM_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q06 - Morphological distinctions between liverworts and mosses

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: The plant body of a liverwort like Marchantia is thalloid, dorsiventral, and closely appressed to the substrate.

Statement II: Gemmae in liverworts are green, multicellular, asexual buds developed in gemma cups.

Statement III: The protonema stage of a moss develops directly from a germinating spore as a creeping, green, branched stage.

Statement IV: The sporophyte of liverworts is structurally far more elaborate than that of mosses.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Statement
Liverworts such as Marchantia feature flattened, dorsiventral thalli that grow closely adhered to the soil.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Asexual reproduction in Marchantia occurs via multicellular green asexual buds known as gemmae produced in dorsal gemma cups.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Moss spores germinate into a filamentous juvenile stage termed the protonema, from which upright leafy gametophores arise.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement and Synthesis
The sporophyte of mosses is structurally more elaborate than that of liverworts, featuring complex capsule differentiation and peristome teeth for spore dispersal.

Final Answer:
The first, second, and third statements are correct, while the fourth statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_KINGDOM_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q07 - Vascular traits and reproductive habits in pteridophytes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: Pteridophytes are evolutionarily the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues, xylem and phloem.

Statement II: The dominant phase in the life cycle of pteridophytes is the sporophyte, which is differentiated into true root, stem, and leaves.

Statement III: The gametophytic prothallus of pteridophytes is a free-living, inconspicuous, and mostly photosynthetic thallus.

Statement IV: Genera such as Selaginella and Salvinia produce only a single kind of spore and are strictly homosporous.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Statement
Pteridophytes mark the evolutionary appearance of internal vascular conducting tissues (xylem and phloem) in land plants.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Unlike bryophytes, the dominant phase in pteridophytes is the diploid sporophyte with differentiated true vegetative organs.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Spore germination produces a small, multicellular, free-living thalloid gametophyte called the prothallus requiring damp environments.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement and Synthesis
Selaginella and Salvinia produce two distinct kinds of spores (microspores and megaspores) and are heterosporous, not homosporous.

Final Answer:
The first, second, and third statements are correct, while the fourth statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_KINGDOM_STATEMENT_BASED_4_Q08 - Gymnosperm ovule morphology mycorrhizae and reproduction

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: In gymnosperms, ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilisation.

Statement II: Pinus roots exhibit mycorrhizal association with fungi, while Cycas possesses coralloid roots associated with cyanobacteria.

Statement III: Gymnosperms are heterosporous, producing haploid microspores and megaspores within specialized sporangia.

Statement IV: In gymnosperms, male and female gametophytes lead an independent free-living existence outside the parent sporophyte.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Statement
Gymnosperms are naked-seeded plants because ovules are borne exposed on sporophylls without an enclosing ovary wall.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Tap roots in Pinus form symbiotic mycorrhizae, whereas Cycas roots develop specialized coralloid roots harboring nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Statement
All gymnosperms are heterosporous, forming microspores in microsporangiate cones and megaspores within ovules.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Fourth Statement and Synthesis
Unlike bryophytes and ferns, gymnosperm gametophytes lack an independent free-living existence and remain retained within sporangia on the sporophyte.

Final Answer:
The first, second, and third statements are correct, while the fourth statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only are correct
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only are correct
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only are correct
